text:
Sarah M: morning handoff — primary for next 8h is Ajay K, secondary is Maria L. I'm handing off an ongoing low-level alert bucket for `svc-cache` but nothing customer-impacting right now.
Ajay K: got it, taking primary. Quick status: what buckets should I watch first?
Sarah M: priority list: 1) API 5xx spike (runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/api-5xx), 2) high tail latency (https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-investigation), 3) mem pressure on worker pools. I've pasted recent alert summary below.
Incident Bot: [ALERT] api-gateway-5xx-rate increased to 6.8% (threshold 1%) — page: P1 if sustained > 3m.
Ajay K: I see the alert feed. Is this customer-facing traffic or internal health checks?
Sarah M: looks real — mobile and web spikes. No incident bridge yet. If it persists > 3m we should page per the matrix. See paging rules: https://redwood.internal/paging-matrix (TL;DR: P1 page primary then call 2min after ack, escalate to secondary at 10m if no ack, manager at 20m).
Maria L: looping in product pager in case support sees customer incidents — @Product Pager can you confirm any high-severity tickets?
Product Pager: there are 2 open tickets reporting errors from Europe, both WindhamCorp integrations. Severity flagged high; customers seeing errors since 06:12 UTC.
Ajay K: ok that suggests customer impact. I'll triage. First step: confirm graph and recent deploys. Sarah — any deploys in last 30m?
Sarah M: no deploys. Last rollout was 02:40 UTC. Monitoring shows CPU on api-gateway pods is normal; error traces show 502-503 from upstream `model-router`.
Leo T: fwiw I just saw a warning in router logs about connection resets to model-serving instances. Pasting quick grep: ```bash
kubectl logs -l app=model-router -n prod --tail=100 | grep "connection reset" | head -n 5
2026-03-14T06:13:11Z model-router-3 connection reset by peer 10.4.6.12:52344
2026-03-14T06:13:12Z model-router-1 connection reset by peer 10.4.6.15:52344
```
Ajay K: thanks Leo. This looks like backend model nodes dropping. I'm going to page per P1 rules. Paging now: @Maria L you're secondary.
Incident Bot: Paging Sequence: page_primary(Ajay K) -> wait 2m -> call_primary -> if no ack escalate to secondary.
Ajay K: acknowledged. I'm on it, creating incident bridge: https://redwood.incident/bridges/1766504321
Maria L: acknowledged, standing by for escalation and context.
Ajay K: triage steps I'm running: 1) check model-serving node health (kubectl get pods -n models), 2) check autoscale logs, 3) verify network ACLs for node group. If model nodes are flapping, we'll failover to warm pool.
Maria L: runbooks: models-flapping (https://redwood.internal/runbooks/models-flapping) and pager-escalation (https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pager-escalation). Also note SLOs — if >3% error for 5m we tag P1 in incident board.
Leo T: I'm looking at node pool logs — found oom_kill on two nodes ~06:08 UTC: ```
[    6.078123] oom_reaper: reaped process 23842 (python) total_vms=120000
```
Ajay K: that matches timing. Could be memory regression on recent model snapshot rollout (but Sarah said no deploys). Maybe autoscaler replaced nodes with new images earlier.
Sarah M: ops infra did a rolling kernel update on that node group at 05:50 UTC (scheduled). Might be correlation.
Ajay K: mitigation plan: spin up warm-pool model instances in eu1, update service routing to drain affected instances, and temporarily increase memory limit for model pods. I'm executing now.
Incident Bot: [BRIDGE CREATED] bridge/1766504321 created by Ajay K — join: https://redwood.incident/bridges/1766504321
Ajay K: executed: `kubectl scale deploy model-warmpool --replicas=6 -n models` and `kubectl patch deploy model-serving -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"worker","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"8Gi"}}}]}}}}' -n models` (monitoring logs).
Maria L: while you do that I'll notify support runbook and update customers via status page if errors persist >10m. Also prepare escalation to SRE manager if we hit paging threshold.
Product Pager: support update template ready: "We are investigating elevated errors affecting API requests; working on mitigation. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes."
Ajay K: good. Quick note on escalation: if primary ack but we need manager involvement (contractual SLA hit, security implication) then page SRE Manager and Prod Lead. Otherwise keep on-call+sre ICs looped.
Sarah M: also add in-cost-control: if warmpool spin-up will blow committed capacity, notify infra-costs slack channel.
Leo T: warmpool came up, I'm seeing connections stable to 6 new nodes. Errors trending down.
Incident Bot: [ALERT RESOLVED] api-gateway-5xx-rate returned to baseline 0.6% — automated alert cleared.
Ajay K: errors dropping, continuing to monitor for 30m. I'll update incident bridge notes and set a postmortem action item: verify kernel update scheduling doesn't overlap with warm pool maintenance.
Maria L: handing notice: Ajay you'll remain primary for another hour if you're OK, then I'll take over. Document in handoff: checklist (acknowledge alerts, confirm bridging, mitigation steps, customer comms link, postmortem owner). Runbook snippet: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/handoff-checklist
Ajay K: fine with that. Final status: customer impact observed (WindhamCorp), temporary mitigation applied, follow-up PM/infra action item created.
Sarah M: thanks everyone. Closing handoff thread — keep alerts muted for noise and tag this oncall record. :thumbsup:
